what: Clean Harbors collects, treats and burns hazardous waste in North America, runs emergency spill response, and through Safety-Kleen collects used oil and re-refines it into new lubricants.
customers: Refineries, chemical plants, manufacturers, hospitals and government agencies, mostly on recurring service contracts.
money: hazardous waste disposal, incineration, industrial cleaning and spill response
used oil collection and re-refined base oil
moat: Permits. Hazardous waste incinerators and landfills take years and heavy opposition to permit, so the existing network is close to impossible to rebuild.
risks: Industrial production drives waste volumes, so a manufacturing slowdown is felt directly
Base oil prices set what the Safety-Kleen half earns, and they move with crude
An incident at an incinerator or landfill carries regulatory and reputational cost well beyond the cleanup
opportunities: Analysts see about 28% upside and the shares trade at 13 times EBITDA
Revenue grew from $3.8B to $6.0B in four years, much of it from acquisitions in a fragmented market
New rules on PFAS, the so-called forever chemicals, create disposal demand that only permitted incinerators can meet
watch: Incineration utilisation and the price per pound of hazardous waste.
